steps.text: Place chocolate chips in a microwave-safe bowl; microwave in 30-second intervals, stirring after each interval, until melted. Do not overheat or chocolate will scorch.
Pierce marshmallows with a toothpick or fork; dip into chocolate. Place on waxed paper or aluminum foil; freeze. Set aside marshmallows at room temperature before serving for 5 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Chocolate-Covered Marshmallows
raw_recipe.description: This chocolate-covered marshmallow recipe yields giant marshmallows dipped in melted chocolate and chilled to make an impressive, sweet, and fluffy treat.
raw_recipe.name: Chocolate-Covered Marshmallows

review.reviewBody: I love making these! I don't like to use chocolate chips - as the liquid firms up too quickly. Chocolate chips have an added agent in them to keep its shape - I use regular melting chocolate instead which melts to a thinner consistency and remains "wetter" longer than melted chocolate chips. I dip the marshmallows 1/2 way in the chocolate and then sprinkle them with rainbow sprinkles. It is always a big hit! Sometimes I also add some pink marshmallows.

Such a fun treat to make! I made them on a stick for my grandchildren for a Valentine's Day treat. I also used the heart shaped marshmallows, dipped them halfway, let them harden up a bit, and then drizzled white chocolate on top.

Made this with my daughter and granddaughter as a Christmas activity. So much fun to do! I had originally gotten soft peppermint sticks, but they were too large to insert into marshmallows but were perfect to crush. Crushed about 15 sticks. Bought the mini candy canes that come 100 to a box to insert. Used 40 of them which matched the number of marshmallows. I would include the peppermints into the ingredients for the recipe. We used a large bag (40) of marshmallows and a 24 oz bag of semi-sweet chocolate chips. We had a little chocolate and crushed peppermint left over that we made peppermint bark out of .
I just made these for my daughter to take to a party ( 10 year olds girls night). I used pretzels for the sticks and dipped the chocolate in crushed Butterfingers for a totally edible treat!

I thought these were great! It was a little too much marshmallow for us, so I cut them in half. I melted chocolate bark in the microwave (stirring every 30 seconds) and dipped the marshmallow halves in the melted chocolate. Then into graham cracker crumbs, like Jeannette H. suggested. They were like little smore bites! We'll definitely be making them again!

My kids and I were looking for something fun to do with Kraft's new Vanilla-Caramel marshmallows. This was an incredibly simple cooking project we could all do together to make everyone happy. We doubled the recipe easily and dipped the chocolate-covered marshmallows in chopped peanuts. The kids are WAY happy and think I'm a total rockstar. All with minimal ingredients. Thanks!

Good and simple. Place the bowl of melted chocolate over a pan of simmering water to keep it at a good consistency. Using a deep Pyrex bowl to dip in worked better than my shallow double boiler. I also used the edge of a rubber spatula to even out and smooth sides and bottom of the marshmallows . . . it only takes a second. . .

Made these for my daughter's valentine treats for her to hand out at school. Put the marshmallows on a popsicle stick dipped them in melted chocolate and sprinkled them with valentine sprinkles. They set up nice and I was able to bag them, add a ribbon and her valentine card. So simple and the kids LOVED them!

Simple, pretty and delicious! I tried dipping the whole marshmallow in the chocolate, but that was so messy and difficult to get the excess chocolate off. So ulitimately, I found that dipping half of the marshmallow in the chocolate was the easiest! I then set them upright and sprinkled colored sprinkles on top. I used Christina's suggestion of using strawberry marshmallows and they are fantastic! The perfect little bite-sized dessert. I love the idea of using graham cracker crumbs, so I will have to try that next time!

An easy, sweet treat! I used heart shaped marshmallows, and half dipped some and did a chocolate drizzle on others, and used some Valentine's Day sprinkles to make it festive. They are so pretty, and tasty too!

Cute and tasty! Made these for a quick addition to my Valentine's Day goodies for friends and neighbors. Dipped about 1/3 of the marshmallow into semisweet chocolate, then sprinkled nonpariels on some. On the others I added some strawberry extract to the chocolate, allowed the chocolate to harden, then drizzled pink-tinted white chocolate over them. Cute! Thanks :)

Delish and so easy. Trying out simple treat recipes in preparation for the holidays. I used chocolate candy squares, which I already had, instead of the chips. I melted the squares and followed the rest of the recipe and they came out just fine. Very reasonable on the budget.
I made this for the holidays when all the family was here, as something fun and different for the kids. They didn't last long and the kids loved them. Fun recipe!
Didn't use sprinkles on top. Had so many my daughter put 1 on a graham cracker, put it in microwave for 8 seconds, put another cracker on top and we had s'mores. Delicious.
Fun and easy! The kids want me to make these again when it gets colder out to drop in their hot chocolate. It's such a simple recipe the kids were able to help dip them.
Really easy! I rolled the dipped marshmallows in finely crushed graham crackers to give it more of a s'more affect.
Cute holiday idea

Very simple to make and allows for creativity. I used a glass cup, kabob sticks and had different types of sprinkles to make these for my family on valentines day one year. I also made the pretzel turtles, chocolate dipped pretzel sticks and the chocolate covered strawberries. (also on this site) It made for a nice presentation. We make these every now and again for special occasions.
Insert mini candy canes for holiday fun. Made them easy to pick up!
easy and a hit with kids! as others recommended I used the bakers chocolate, melted in the microwave and then put the dipped marshmallows in the freezer for 10 minutes.
